newsitem.title: ITALY: Van Mierlo urges political solution in Albania.
newsitem.headline: Van Mierlo urges political solution in Albania.

text.p: Dutch Foreign Minister Hans Van Mierlo called on Thursday for a political solution to Albania's bloody crisis as he prepared for a European Union mission to Tirana to meet President Sali Berisha and the opposition.

Van Mierlo, whose country holds the EU's rotating presidency, said he would deliver a "clear message" to all sides in his talks on Friday that they must find a common line on how to secure a peaceful end to armed insurrection in the south.
"We should do this in the interest of Albania (but) it's in the interest of Europe also that we do everything to get a political solution in Albania," Van Mierlo said.
He also made clear that future economic aid from the EU, the impoverished Balkan state's biggest source of funds, would depend on Albanian willingness to refrain from violence.

"We want to help but they must make it possible and there should be an underlying agreement between the European Union and Albania on the line to follow," Van Mierlo told a joint news conference with Italian Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini.
"That is a prerequisite for the attitude of the European Union," he said.
Van Mierlo, who was due to meet Greek Prime Minister Costas Simitis in Athens later on Thursday, declined to specify what advice he would give Berisha and the 11-party opposition Forum for Democracy.

But he said Dutch thinking was "very much on the same line" as that of Italy, which has called for a government of national reconciliation in the former Stalinist state pending an early general election.
Dini said there had been numerous contacts between Berisha and his ruling Democratic Party and the opposition, whose main force is the Socialist Party.

"The situation is rapidly changing and therefore we should not exclude that some form of agreement can be reached before too long," Dini said. He said Berisha had assured Italy that he would not use military force to re-take rebel towns.
Van Mierlo said it was "reassuring" that Berisha had offered the opposition an election deal last week. "That is a point of departure," he said.
In Tirana, members of political parties from the right and left, including the Democrats and Socialists, were seen by reporters entering the presidency building on Thursday morning.

It was not immediately clear whether they were to meet Berisha. Parliament, which has declared a state of emergency and re-elected Berisha to a second five-year term as president, had also been convened.

Berisha removed the government of Prime Minister Aleksander Meksi on Saturday as weeks of protests sparked by the collapse of shady pyramid investment schemes exploded into an armed uprising in the south of the country.
But opposition parties, demoralised since the state of emergency measures were introduced, seek the establishment of a broad-based government before early elections.
Van Mierlo will be the first senior Western minister to visit Albania since Sunday's introduction of emergency rule.
He said he would also urge Berisha to accept a visit from the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE).

Austrian former chancellor Franz Vranitzky, who has been named to lead the OSCE mission, said on Thursday the exact timing remained open but that he and Berisha had agreed it would take place at the earliest possible moment.
